title: Code Generation and Runtime Systems
description: Instruction selection, register allocation, ABIs, and the runtime that still exists after the compiler is done — including JIT.

sourceReferences.title: Stanford CS143
sourceReferences.notes: Codegen, register allocation, GC, JIT as later phases.

sourceReferences.title: CMU 15-411/611
sourceReferences.notes: Instruction selection and the backend as first-class work.

sourceReferences.title: System V AMD64 ABI
sourceReferences.notes: One concrete calling convention and frame layout.

sourceReferences.title: Java Virtual Machine Specification
sourceReferences.notes: Runtime, GC roots, and compiling while the program already runs.

modules.title: Selection and allocation
learningObjectives: Turn an IR operator into target opcodes
Pack live values into the real register file

modules.title: Talking to the platform
learningObjectives: Place arguments where the platform requires
Leave a frame the callee and the unwinder can both read

modules.title: Runtimes and JITs
learningObjectives: Find live objects without a matching free()
Compile a hot fragment while the program is already running

concepts.name: Instruction selection
concepts.summary: IR operators become real opcodes.
objectives: Replace an IR operator with one or more target opcodes that implement it
Compare two legal selections and say what makes one cheaper

concepts.name: Register allocation
concepts.summary: Graph coloring, spilling, and the real cost of an extra live range.
objectives: Assign interfering live ranges to different registers or to memory
Predict when the interference graph forces a spill

concepts.name: Spilling
concepts.summary: A value that did not fit, living on the stack.
objectives: Insert a store and later reload because no register is free
Predict the extra memory traffic a spill adds to a hot loop

concepts.name: Instruction scheduling
concepts.summary: Reordering to hide latency without breaking dependences.
objectives: Reorder independent instructions to hide latency without breaking dependences
Diagnose a schedule that moves a load before the store it depends on

concepts.name: Peephole opts
concepts.summary: Tiny local rewrites on the real ISA.
objectives: Rewrite a short window of target instructions into a cheaper equivalent
State why a peephole must preserve the window's observable effect

concepts.name: Calling conventions
concepts.summary: Which arguments live in which registers.
objectives: Place arguments and the return value where the platform's convention requires
Predict which registers a caller must save across a call

concepts.name: Stack frames
concepts.summary: The record a call leaves behind.
objectives: Describe the stack frame a prologue builds and an epilogue tears down
Trace where a spilled value and a return address sit in the frame

concepts.name: Object files
concepts.summary: Sections, symbols, and what the linker will see.
objectives: Name the sections and symbols an object file shows the linker
Predict what is still unknown inside a .o that the linker must finish

concepts.name: Relocations
concepts.summary: Addresses the linker still has to fill in.
objectives: Describe a relocation as a hole the linker fills with a final address
Predict what breaks if a relocation is applied at the wrong width or place

concepts.name: Linking
concepts.summary: Many objects, one address space.
objectives: Combine object files by resolving symbols and applying relocations
Diagnose an undefined reference as a symbol no object provided

concepts.name: Position-independent code
concepts.summary: Code that does not assume where it was loaded.
objectives: Generate an address using a relative load so the code can sit anywhere
Predict why an absolute immediate is illegal in a shared library

concepts.name: Thread-local storage
concepts.summary: A global that is not shared.
objectives: Describe thread-local storage as a global name with one cell per thread
Predict what goes wrong if two threads share an ordinary global instead

concepts.name: Debug info
concepts.summary: DWARF as a map back to the source the optimizer scrambled.
objectives: Map an optimized location back to a source span the human still recognizes
Predict why a dead store's variable may have no current location

concepts.name: The language runtime
concepts.summary: The support code every compiled program still links.
objectives: Name support the compiled program still links after the compiler finishes
Distinguish a language runtime from the OS kernel

concepts.name: Automatic memory management
concepts.summary: Finding the live objects without a free().
objectives: Find live objects from roots without a matching free()
Compare a conservative scan with a precise one that needs stack maps

concepts.name: Exceptions
concepts.summary: Unwinding until someone catches.
objectives: Unwind frames until a matching handler is found
Predict which destructors or cleanups run on the way out

concepts.name: Stack unwinding
concepts.summary: Tables instead of a setjmp in every frame.
objectives: Use unwind tables instead of a setjmp in every frame
Explain why tables stay off the hot path until an exception is thrown

concepts.name: Stack maps
concepts.summary: Where the GC roots are at this safepoint.
objectives: Record where GC roots live at a safepoint
Predict what the collector gets wrong if a root is missing from the map

concepts.name: JIT compilation
concepts.summary: Compiling while the program runs.
objectives: Compile a hot fragment while the program is already running
Compare JIT compile-time cost with the speed the new code must repay

concepts.name: Deoptimization
concepts.summary: Falling back when a speculative type was a lie.
objectives: Fall back to a safer version when a speculative assumption is false
Predict the state the interpreter or baseline compiler must reconstruct

concepts.name: Link-time optimization
concepts.summary: Seeing the whole program after the .o files exist.
objectives: Optimize across object-file boundaries after the linker can see the whole program
Compare LTO with a compile-time IPO that never saw the other .o

concepts.name: Profile-guided optimization
concepts.summary: Letting yesterday's run tell today's inliner the truth.
objectives: Use yesterday's profile to decide today's inlining and layout
Predict a mis-optimization when the profile does not match this run
